approach: In gh.rs replace_early (the one place the landing commit overwrites the early head, called from publish and land_pr), add a bounded wait before job.remote.replace. It runs only when an early head exists and differs from the landing commit. It polls host.ci_runs(early_head) every 20s step, sleeping through job.poll.sleep. It stops when the runs are non-empty and all completed, or when the summed sleeps reach the bound. Failed runs, no runs, or a ci_runs error stop it at once. The bound comes from a new default method on the PrHost trait (10 minutes), so no LandPr or Poll field is added and no struct literal elsewhere has to change. Test fakes override it with a small value. replace_early returns a one-line note (seconds waited, reason) that publish and land_pr append to the report's existing warnings.

decisions.choice: Bound lives in a default method PrHost::early_run_wait() -> Duration (10 min); wait step is a const 20s; sleeping uses the injected job.poll.sleep.
decisions.reason: Adding a LandPr field would break literals in run_pin_tests.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests/external_calls.rs, which are outside the deliverables (findings 2 and 3). A trait default method needs no literal changes, keeps production at 10 minutes, and lets a fake host inject a small bound so tests never really sleep.

rejected.why: Breaks every LandPr literal, including two files outside the deliverables.
Poll also drives the pages and checks waits, and has literals too.
land.rs only plans and classifies; it does not push.

rejected.option: Filter runs by the name 'fmt, clippy, tests'
rejected.why: CiRunState has no name field and no new host call is wanted; waiting for all runs of the commit is a safe superset because of the bound.

decisions.choice: Failure, timed_out, empty runs, or a ci_runs error end the wait at once and the push proceeds as today.
decisions.reason: Only a pending run can produce a cached pass worth waiting for; all else must leave merging unchanged.

rejected.option: Retry on ci_runs error until timeout
rejected.why: Delays landing with nothing to gain.

decisions.choice: Report the note through the existing warnings in the report; land.rs and run.rs stay unchanged unless the compiler requires otherwise.
decisions.reason: Smallest change; the wait is in the push path in gh.rs.

rejected.why: Widens the public type for a log line.

files.purpose: Add PrHost::early_run_wait default method, step const, wait_for_early_run; call it in replace_early; surface the note in publish and land_pr; add tests and override the bound in test fakes.
Only if shared fakes need a scripted ci_runs and event log for the new tests; otherwise unchanged.
Entry for the wait, saying the next real landing's time is still to be measured.
Expected unchanged: it plans and classifies and does no pushing. Touch only if the compiler requires it.
Expected unchanged: no LandPr change is needed. Touch only if the compiler requires it.

steps: Read PrHost (gh.rs ~407), replace_early (~1991), publish (~2006), land_pr, the report warnings type, and the test fakes (~2898) and test_support.rs.
Add const EARLY_RUN_STEP (20s) and default const EARLY_RUN_WAIT (10 min) and the default method PrHost::early_run_wait.

Write wait_for_early_run(job, early_head) -> String: loop on ci_runs; Err, empty, or any failed/timed_out run returns a note at once; all completed returns a note; elapsed >= bound returns a timed-out note; else job.poll.sleep(step) and add the step.
Call it in replace_early before check_replace and the push; return the note to publish and land_pr and append it to the report warnings.
Add the tests for criteria 1-4 and 6 with a shared event log among the fake host, fake remote and recording sleep; the fake host overrides early_run_wait.
Add the CHANGELOG entry with the pending-measurement wording.
Run cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: Existing fakes returning in_progress now loop through the 10 minute bound (30 injected sleeps) and might assert sleep counts.
risks.mitigation: Override early_run_wait to ZERO in those fakes; sleeps are injected so there is no real delay.

risks.risk: Production landing is delayed up to 10 minutes if the early run hangs.
risks.mitigation: The wait is bounded and falls through to a push as today.

risks.risk: Waiting on all runs of the commit may wait on unrelated slow workflows.
risks.mitigation: The bound caps it; the open question names it.

risks.risk: The measured landing time is not available in this job.
risks.mitigation: The CHANGELOG marks it pending and names the source to record (PR number, run timestamps).

demonstrations.method: Fake-host test: ci_runs on the early commit returns in_progress twice, then completed/success. A recording sleep and the fake remote share an event log.
demonstrations.observes: The log shows three ci_runs calls on the early commit with sleeps between them, and the replace push logged after the last ci_runs call.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the wait the push is logged before any ci_runs call or sleep, so the ordering assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Fake ci_runs returns a completed run on the first call.
demonstrations.observes: One ci_runs call, zero sleep calls, the push happens, and the note says already completed.
demonstrations.fails_without: A wait that sleeps before checking records a sleep and fails the zero-sleep assertion.

demonstrations.method: Fake host overrides early_run_wait to 60s; ci_runs always returns in_progress; recording sleep does not block. A second assertion checks the trait default is 10 minutes.
demonstrations.observes: Recorded sleeps total at least 60s and at most 60s plus one step, the landing push still happens, and the note says timed out.
demonstrations.fails_without: An unbounded wait never returns (the fake caps calls and fails); without the fall-through the landing commit is not pushed.

demonstrations.method: Table of cases (failed run, timed_out run, empty run list, ci_runs Err). Each runs land_pr through merge and compares merge calls and the report with a baseline run with no early-head wait.
demonstrations.observes: No sleeps, the push happens, merge is called with the landing commit, and the report matches the baseline apart from the note.
demonstrations.fails_without: A wait that treats failure as pending sleeps to the bound; one that propagates the ci_runs error aborts the landing.

demonstrations.method: Run the whole suite, including the new tests of criteria 1-4 and the existing land_pr and publish tests, which stay unmodified because no struct literal changes. Then clippy and fmt.
demonstrations.observes: All tests pass, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` exit clean.
demonstrations.fails_without: The new tests of criteria 1-4 are in this run and fail without the wait; a broken existing land_pr or publish test (for example one that now sleeps or errors on ci_runs) fails the same run.

demonstrations.method: Check the note for each stop reason, and cases with no early head and with early head equal to the landing commit.
demonstrations.observes: The note contains seconds waited and the reason (completed, already completed, no runs, ci_runs error, timed out). With no early head or equal heads there are zero ci_runs calls and no note.
demonstrations.fails_without: A wait that runs unconditionally calls ci_runs in the no-early-head case and fails the zero-call assertion.

demonstrations.observes: The entry describes the wait and the race (PR #180: early run passed 10:46:49, landing run started 10:45:15), states the next real landing's time is still to be measured with no new number, and says to record it with its PR number and run timestamps once observed.

open_questions: CiRunState has no workflow name, so the wait covers all runs of the early commit, not only 'fmt, clippy, tests'.
Whether existing fake hosts report in_progress and assert sleep counts; if so those tests must override early_run_wait to ZERO in the fake.
The real landing time cannot be measured in this job; the CHANGELOG records it as pending.
